kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Section 1] One drinks the second cup and does not bless on it, etc. In Tur he brought a dispute on this: per the Rif one must bless borei peri hagafen, and his reason is because the four cups — since each one is a commandment by itself — one must bless borei peri hagafen on every cup and cup. And so is the opinion of Rav Nissim Gaon, Rav Amram, Rambam, and Ravyah, that one must bless on every cup and cup. But the Rosh wrote on the words of the Rif mentioned, that it is not clear: for even though each one is a commandment by itself, since there is no distraction of attention, one need not bless borei peri hagafen except on the first cup, which is for kiddush, and on the third, which is for Birkat Hamazon; but on the second and on the fourth one need not bless — and so too Rav Kohen Tzedek. And Beit Yosef wrote: and so they practiced, not to bless borei peri hagafen except on the cup of kiddush and cup of Birkat Hamazon — end of his words. And such are his words here in Shulchan Aruch. And so is Sephardic custom.
rabbi-akiva-eiger/1:_: Magen Avraham note 1: on each one — in Mordechai: since each one, for its word, was enacted — he diverts his attention from it until its time arrives.
